name: Vynaris
summary: OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API gateway that routes each request to a cheaper model when evals allow it, with a receipt per request showing the model and cost. Prepaid credit, no overages.
best_for: developers running agents or apps on OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible APIs who want requests routed to cheaper models where that is safe, with a receipt per request to check the savings
skip_if: you need an established vendor with a track record and compliance paperwork, always want one specific model, or cannot send traffic through a third-party gateway
honest_knock: It is an early beta, and the savings figures on the homepage are the vendor's own; it says live routing statistics are still to be published. The routing fee comes on top of the model price, so if routing rarely picks a cheaper model you pay slightly more than calling the provider directly. Your traffic passes through a third party, which matters for compliance. The hosted uncensored models are aimed at authorised security testing only.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-04 on vynaris.com/pricing, US dollars) Vynaris is an API gateway, so what you pay is mostly the price of the models it calls for you. Every routed request is billed at the original provider list price of the model that actually served it, plus a Vynaris fee of 3% on your first $500 of usage in a month and 1% on the rest of that month; a $500 top-up switches to the 1% rate at once for that calendar month. You fund it with prepaid top-ups from $20 by card or stablecoins; credit does not expire, and requests stop when the balance reaches zero, so there are no overages. Instead of top-ups you can take a fixed plan whose payment becomes API credit: S at $20 a month, L at $50 a month and XL at $150 a month, with unused credit rolling over. L and XL also give access to Vynaris' own hosted uncensored models, priced per token from $1 per million input tokens, and allow payment in Monero at a 20% surcharge. On 10 November 2026 the pricing page listed four of those hosted “reduced-refusal” models, all with 128K context: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B at $1 per million input tokens ($5 and $7 output), DeepSeek-V4-Flash at $2 / $11 and GLM-5.3 at $5 / $20. The page promises “no prompt or output retention” for them; that is the vendor's statement, which we have not tested. The site labels the service an early beta.

schema_offer.description: S plan, fixed monthly plan that adds $20 of API credit each month; pay-as-you-go alternative is the provider list price plus a 3% routing fee on the first $500 of monthly usage and 1% after that, with prepaid top-ups from $20; L $50 and XL $150 a month. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-04.

cost_traps.evidence: Instead of top-ups you can take a fixed plan whose payment becomes API credit: S at $20 a month, L at $50 a month and XL at $150 a month, with unused credit rolling over.

compare_with.name: Direct provider APIs
compare_with.why: Calling OpenAI or Anthropic directly costs the provider list price with no routing fee. Vynaris charges that same list price plus 3% on the first $500 a month (1% after) and in return routes requests to cheaper models when its evals allow it and shows the cost of every request
